title: Screen never turns off after automatic lock when "When locked, turn off screen" equals the dim timeout
line: After an automatic lock the screen now turns off after the "When locked, turn off screen" delay even when dimming uses the same delay
explanation: When the screen locks, PowerDevil's DPMS action adds a new idle timeout for "When locked, turn off screen" and expects it to count from the lock. KIdleTime gives every addIdleTimeout() call its own identifier, but its Wayland poller kept only one idle notification per length, so a second timeout of the same length (dimming's) was folded into the existing one: if that had already gone idle the screen never turned off, otherwise it turned off counted from the last input rather than from the lock. KIdleTime now lets a poller key its timeouts by registration identifier through a small optional interface, and the Wayland poller uses it: each addIdleTimeout() gets its own ext-idle-notify notification that counts from when it was added, and removeIdleTimeout() frees only that one. Pollers that don't implement it (X11, Windows, macOS, KWin's own) keep the old per-length path, which suits them because they measure one global idle time anyway.

commits.message:
wayland: give each idle timeout its own notification

Timeouts of the same length shared one Wayland idle notification, so a
new one counted from when the first was added, or never fired if that
had already gone idle. Pollers can now key timeouts by registration id.

BUG: 527667

media.caption: Pure master, 4x speed: a same-length idle action fires at 30 s, the session auto-locks at 60 s with 'when locked, turn off screen' 30 s, and the lock screen stays lit to the end (150 s)
Same steps with the KIdleTime fix: the screen turns off at 90 s idle, 30 s after the lock
Pure master at 144 s idle: still on, 54 s after it should have turned off
With the fix at 144 s idle: off since 90 s

review.text: The cause is in KIdleTime, as it should be: the Wayland poller folded same-length timeouts into one ext-idle-notify notification, so a timeout added later (DPMS on lock) didn't count from when it was added. An optional qobject_cast interface keyed by registration id keeps KWin's own poller plugin binary-compatible, and PowerDevil needs no change. Small nits for the MR: Wayland Poller::timeouts() now returns identifiers rather than lengths (unused, but misleading), and the no-op addTimeout/removeTimeout could say why in one place. The before/after videos and the same-length and different-length regression checks show the fix clearly.
